correctness.rationale: For arbitrary domain and team, induct on m to find finite failure; in a minimal failure every one-point deletion has a covering tuple, yielding a rational nonzero diagonal interpolation matrix. The rank is bounded by the dimension 2^m of the multilinear polynomials. The Boolean cube is a size-2^m minimally failing witness. The verified program exhaustively checks all binary m<=4 and ternary m<=2 teams and cube interpolation diagonals m<=6. The proof, not these checks, establishes the infinite-domain statement.

originality.rationale: The known two-constancy width-four case is explicitly excluded from novelty. Primary full text of 2025/2026 papers and independent semantic searches did not establish the sharp uniform all-m width over arbitrary alphabets. Qualitative existence of some coherence bound and a trivial binary-domain size bound do not imply the quantitative domain-independent 2^m theorem. A more general interpolation or coordinate-cover theorem could subsume it and remains the historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: A historically prior generic interpolation/Helly theorem on coordinate-parallel covers may subsume the unbounded-alphabet obstruction-width result under a different name.
Not every older publication on team logic and covering arrays could be read exhaustively; historical priority is not independently certified.

The two cited papers sometimes describe coherence via exactly k-element subteams; the new claim explicitly uses the unambiguous at-most-k obstruction invariant and does not assert a literal exact-size test on smaller teams.

value.rationale: Provides an exact sharp natural local obstruction invariant for a syntactically fundamental family of dependence-logic formulas over arbitrary universes. Unlike a trivial bound on binary teams, it is independent of alphabet cardinality and supplies an explicit certificate and new m>=3 exact levels. The magnitude and sharp Boolean-cube extremizers are meaningful for finite-obstruction first-order translations.
